operations.text: 0.2.5 changes three things the loop DOES, and all three travel with /plugin update rather than with this migration: the doctrine your session reads is the payload's own docs/ and skills/, which are replaced wholesale by the plugin update. First, a Reviewer or QA verdict now reaches you as the verdict plus one or two sentences of its substance, before the next dispatch step - never a bare 'pass, moving on', which is how an audit you paid for used to disappear on the way to the next dispatch. Second, and this one costs money in the other direction: the default that let the COO dispatch a later auditor pass on the word you gave for the ticket is REVOKED. Pass 1 of a route rides the ticket's word; every further auditor pass - a further configured readiness pass, the verification pass after a correction round that touched code, a pass beyond the review contract, a round past the correction cap - is dispatched only after you say so, one word per pass. `review.<class>.passes` is from now on a CEILING, not a budget the COO may spend on its own; nothing about the numbers in your audit table changes, only who releases each pass after the first. Third, fail aggregation inside the plan-readiness cycle stops being a bare ban and becomes a mechanism: from pass 2 of such a cycle on, the brief hands the Reviewer the blocker list the previous pass returned, and every new blocker it raises declares why that pass could not see it - one raised without that declaration is reported as a broken contract, separately from the verdict. Two managed artifacts of yours state the revoked default in writing, and both are re-rendered here: the `aiwf-core` region of your CLAUDE.md, whose operator-gates paragraph carried it in one line, and - where one was ever rendered - `.claude/agents/reviewer.md`, whose plan-readiness section described the configured passes as granted and only the one beyond them as needing your word. A Claude-hosted Reviewer reads that agent file rather than the doctrine, so leaving it would hand the auditor the revoked model. The same re-render also carries the third change above into that agent, in its own voice, because the auditor that has to apply it is the one reading that file rather than the doctrine. Your own text outside the CLAUDE.md markers is untouched; a project with a Codex-hosted Reviewer has no reviewer.md and sees that operation reported as skipped; and an artifact you hold through an override is not re-applied at all - the new render is recorded as upstream and the CHANGES report says so.
